gaps.sentence: This smell ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' means to make someone think of something; 'remember' is not followed by an object + of.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
gaps.explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.

gaps.sentence: The money was divided ___ the four children.
gaps.hint: for a group of more than two
gaps.explanation: 'Among' is traditionally used for more than two; 'between' is preferred for exactly two.
'Than' is used in comparisons; 'then' refers to time or consequence.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: Studying abroad is a wonderful ___ to practise your Spanish.
gaps.hint: a situation that lets you do something; pattern: ___ to do
gaps.explanation: 'Opportunity to do something' means a chance a situation gives you; 'possibility' is not followed by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The gallery is open daily ___ Mondays, when it closes for cleaning.
gaps.explanation: 'Except' excludes; 'accept' is the verb for receiving willingly.
